item.title: Former 'Real Housewives' star calls Andy Cohen's political take defending 'MAGA' women 'full of s---'
item.description: Former "RHOC" star Kelly Dodd claimed Andy Cohen was "full of s---" for defending MAGA women on Bravo, claiming they weren't welcome on the show.
item.content:encoded:
Former "Real Housewives of Orange County" star Kelly Dodd claimed that Bravo host Andy Cohen was "full of s---" Tuesday after he defended the inclusion of "MAGA women" on the show.

Dodd spoke to Fox News Digital after the "Watch What Happens Live" host was asked on Threads why there were "so many MAGA women" on the series, particularly the "Orange County" season.

"If we didn’t showcase people with different POV’s there would be no show. Also it’s a show about the women and their relationships, not about politics," Cohen wrote on Sunday.

KELLY DODD FIRES BACK AT CANCEL CULTURE, SAYS SHE'S TREATED LIKE 'AN OUTCAST' IN HOLLYWOOD

Dodd called out this comment, claiming that Cohen and Bravo did not care for conservative perspectives on the show before and have since become concerned only about ratings.

"They're making excuses that they need points of views when I don't think that's true," Dodd said, adding, "He doesn't have different points of view. I think he's full of s---."

Dodd pointed to Cohen's past comments attacking conservatives and right-leaning perspectives and viewed his Threads comment, and the show welcoming different types of women, as disingenuous.

"I think that he sees that the ratings are slipping, and he needs to get back some conservative. He's lost half of his audience. Any time you talk, speak about politics... You're gonna p--- off half the country," Dodd said.

ANDY COHEN BLASTS JOE ROGAN AS A 'F---ING IDIOT' AFTER HE BACKS PRATT FOR LA MAYOR

Cohen, however, agreed that the "Real Housewives" brand was not political in any way and that she herself had not discussed politics prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

"The show is not about politics, it's about women's lives. It's not about politics. No one's running for office or no one's talking about politics," Dodd said.

Bravo and its parent company NBCUniversal declined to comment. 

Fox News Digital also reached out to Cohen's representative for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Dodd was among multiple women who were fired or left the franchise after making controversial comments or criticizing left-wing politics. Dodd was previously fired from the series in 2021 following controversial remarks about the COVID-19 pandemic and accusations of her mocking the Black Lives Matter movement. 

REALITY STAR SAYS 'RHOC' COST HER MARRIAGE AS DAUGHTER SHUNS SHOW AFTER MILITARY HUSBAND'S PORTRAYAL

Former cast member Annemarie Wiley, of "The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills," also spoke to Fox News Digital last year about no longer being invited to the show after leaving in 2024 for expressing conservative views, like protecting girls' sports.

"I was given a terrible edit by Bravo and I found out after the season was finished when they didn't invite me back, that that was the reason that I was given that edit, apparently… because I was a conservative," Wiley told Fox News Digital.

Earlier this year, NBCUniversal boasted that Bravo was "a top cable entertainment network among key female demos" with Q1 2026 scoring Bravo's biggest quarter on the streaming service Peacock.

However, seasons of the "Real Housewives" franchise have reportedly seen declining ratings in recent years.

item.title: John Hinckley Jr gives his thoughts on Jodie Foster 45 years after shooting Ronald Reagan to impress her
item.description: John Hinckley Jr. reveals that Jodie Foster could have been a target herself, saying "fate went the other way" toward former President Ronald Reagan.
item.content:encoded:
John Hinckley Jr., the man who shot former President Ronald Reagan in 1981 to impress Jodie Foster, said he wants nothing but good things for the actress.

"I just wish Jodie Foster well," he said. "I don’t really see her movies, but I wish her well, and I know she’s doing quite well. And that’s all I can say: I just, I wish Jodie well, and I hope she has a good life."

The 71-year-old explained on the "Mark Joseph Show" in an exclusive preview shared with Entertainment Weekly that when he shot Reagan 45 years ago in a delusional state, he believed he would spend the rest of his life with the "Silence of the Lambs" actress.

REAGAN SHOOTER CALLS LINK TO WASHINGTON HOTEL ‘SPOOKY’ AFTER ALLEGED TRUMP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT AT SAME SITE

The full episode will air on Wednesday.

"I wanted to have like this union with Jodie Foster and live the rest of my life with her and all these things that, of course, were delusional, but I was believing those things at that time. So, the best outcome would have been to just have like this union with Jodie Foster," Hinckley told Joseph after the host asked what he believed at the time would be the best thing that could come out of the shooting.

He explained that he believed at the time that Foster would "join me wherever I was. You know, I didn’t know if I was going to be in jail or hospital or what, but after things settled down, I had this notion that she was going to join me wherever I was."

It came out shortly after Hinckley’s assassination attempt that left Reagan with a broken rib, punctured lung and internal bleeding, that Hinckley was obsessed with Foster after seeing her in "Taxi Driver" and thought the shooting would make her notice him.

JODIE FOSTER HAUNTED BY HORRIFIC DOG TRAGEDY, BELIEVES SHE GAVE UP WHAT SHE LOVES MOST FOR SUCCESS

Hinckley was found not guilty by reason of insanity after shooting the former president outside the Washington Hilton two months after he was elected.

Former White House press secretary James Brady was shot in the head and suffered brain damage and partial paralysis, which led to his death in 2014. His death was ruled a homicide.

Two other men were also wounded in the shooting.

Hinckley was committed to a psychiatric hospital after the trial and released in 2016. By 2022, he was living in Virginia without any court restrictions.

Hinckley admitted to Joseph, however, that, in his delusional state, Foster could have been a target herself.

"She definitely could have been a target. It’s just fate went the other way," Hinckley said. "But, yeah, she could have been a target. But, as fate turned out, it was Reagan instead of her."

In a 2022 interview with CBS, Hinckley apologized for his actions.

"I shot four people, and I’m sorry to the Reagan family, the Brady family, the other families of the victims," he said at the time. "I’m sorry to Jodie Foster for bringing her into this."

item.title: Mamdani's team said NYPD would accompany his wife on Middle East vacation — cops say that's not true
item.description: The NYPD denied it would send officers to Syria and Lebanon with Rama Duwaji, contradicting Mayor Zohran Mamdani's office on the security detail.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Police Department (NYPD) will not provide a security detail to Mayor Zohran Mamdani's wife during her upcoming vacation to two terror hotspots in the Middle East, despite the mayor's office claiming otherwise.

"The NYPD does not send officers to countries with level 4 travel advisories for discretionary reasons such as personal travel," a spokesperson for the law enforcement agency told Fox News.

Mamdani's wife, Rama Duwaji, is planning to travel to Syria and Lebanon to visit family in September, according to the New York Post. Both of those countries are on the State Department's "Do Not Travel" list due to terrorism concerns.

MAMDANI'S WIFE CO-HOSTS LUXE MUSLIM RETREAT CASTING VIRGIN MARY AS ‘PALESTINIAN WOMAN’ UNDER OCCUPATION

The mayor's office had previously confirmed that Duwaji would have an NYPD security detail on the trip.

"Upon the strong recommendation of the NYPD, the first lady’s security detail will be joining her when she travels to visit family in Syria and Lebanon," Mamdani’s spokeswoman Dora Pekec reportedly said.

But later, as it became clear that the NYPD would not be making the overseas trek, the mayor chalked the confusion up to a staff "miscommunication" when asked about it by news outlet PIX11 on Tuesday.

NYPD Detectives’ Endowment Association (DEA) President Scott Munro furiously slammed the implication that NYPD detectives would accompany the city's First Lady to the Middle East.

MAMDANI CLASHES WITH DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' PUSH TO ABOLISH POLICE AND PRISONS

"Our detectives put themselves in harm’s way every day protecting New Yorkers," said Munro. "The DEA would never remain silent if our members were asked to travel to a dangerous, off-limits foreign country for anything other than a legitimate law-enforcement or intelligence operation."

"Our detectives are needed here in New York City protecting residents and fighting crime," he added.

Mamdani has a long history of trashing the very police department he thought would accompany and provide security for his wife to the dangerous Middle Eastern countries on New York City taxpayer's dime.

"There is no negotiating with an institution this wicked & corrupt. Defund it. Dismantle it. End the cycle of violence," Mamdani said in reference to the NYPD in a viral 2020 post on X.

"We don't need an investigation to know that the NYPD is racist, anti-queer & a major threat to public safety," he said in another 2020 post, adding in a follow-up: "What we need is to #DefundTheNYPD."

JON STEWART PRESSES MAMDANI ON WHERE HE BREAKS WITH FELLOW DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ON PRISONS AND BORDERS

"Queer liberation means defund the police," he said in yet another post.

The mayor, who has also faced scrutiny for his anti-Israel views and recently called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal" while calling for his arrest, derogatorily linked the NYPD to the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF).

"We have to make clear that when the boot of the NYPD is on your neck, it’s been laced by the IDF," Mamdani, who was a keynote speaker, said during a panel discussion at the Democratic Socialists of America's 2023 national convention.

During his campaign for mayor of the most populated U.S. city, Mamdani said the exact opposite, explicitly stating that he did not want to defund the police.

SEE IT: MAMDANI BOOED OFF STAGE AT NEW YORK CITY PRO-POLICE CELEBRATION: ‘WALKED OFF IN SHAME’

Still, it appears there is no love lost between Mamdani and the NYPD.

Just last week, he was booed offstage when he tried to speak at a pro-police event in Staten Island.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani's office for comment.

item.title: Alex Rodriguez defends Dodgers' spending spree as likely lockout gets closer: 'I think it's great'
item.description: Alex Rodriguez says the Los Angeles Dodgers aren't ruining baseball, comparing their spending to the New York Yankees' payroll dominance in the 2000s.
item.content:encoded:
With a lockout more likely than not at this point in Major League Baseball, the ongoing debate continues over whether the Los Angeles Dodgers are actually ruining the sport.

Many believe the Dodgers have simply broken baseball, particularly with Shohei Ohtani's $700 million contract, 97% of which is deferred. They have won back-to-back World Series titles and are the favorite for a third consecutive title.

Not only did Los Angeles follow up its titles by signing the most touted reliever on the market in Edwin Diaz, but it also gave Kyle Tucker a deal that gave him the highest annual average value of $60 million, the most for any position player ever.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

However, former slugger Alex Rodriguez isn't buying the negativity surrounding the organization.

"I think it’s great. You and I both would be hypocrites if we said it’s not good when we saw what happened in the ‘90s here in New York, what happened in ‘09 when Hal Steinbrenner flexed his financial resources to go out and get [CC] Sabathia, [Mark] Teixeira and A.J. Burnett, and the year before we had Johnny Damon," A-Rod told New York Yankees broadcaster Michael Kay on the latter's radio show.

Rodriguez does make an interesting point — in 2005, the Yankees' payroll ($208.3 million, per Baseball Reference) was almost double the second-highest payroll (the Boston Red Sox's $123.5 million). The New York Mets ($101.3 million) were the only other team to have a nine-digit payroll.

While the Dodgers have finessed their contracts through deferrals and bonuses to make their actual payroll less than the actual value of the contracts, numerous other teams are actually still in the comparative ballpark. The Mets, Philadelphia Phillies and Toronto Blue Jays each have a tax payroll of at least $300 million.

Rodriguez noted that it's not necessarily the amount of money but how it's spent.

FORMER MLB STAR CALLS FOR SALARY FIX AS OWNERS, PLAYERS ASSOCIATION TALK 'TWO DIFFERENT LANGUAGES'

"The key is not making the mistakes..." Rodriguez said, name-dropping Trent Grisham and Ryan McMahon, who are combining to make $38 million this season while hitting a combined .215 with an OPS below .700.

"You have to be able to determine what is your inventory and what is it worth. Gene Michael used to be able to hold on to Bernie [Williams], [Derek] Jeter, [Jorge] Posada. That's the key — you got to hold on to your early guys, and then move on for the others, use them as assets to complement your current roster."

Again, to Rodriguez's point, the Milwaukee Brewers, whose $153 million tax payroll is 19th in the league, own the best record in Major League Baseball. The Tampa Bay Rays rank 27th in tax payroll yet have the league's second-best record, while the AL Central-leading Chicago White Sox rank 26th.

Furthermore, three of the top five payrolls in the sport — the Mets, Phillies and Blue Jays — are currently out of the postseason.

The current collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, and players have insisted they would not play under a salary cap, which has been formally offered for the first time since 1994.

item.title: Dem in key swing race missed nearly half her state House votes while taking taxpayer salary: 'No show'
item.description: Former Iowa Democratic state Rep. Christina Bohannan missed 45% of Iowa House floor votes in 2022 while campaigning for a congressional seat.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Former Democratic state Rep. Christina Bohannan missed nearly half of her votes in Iowa's House of Representatives during her final year in office as she campaigned for a congressional seat in the battleground district, records show.

In 2022, Bohannan missed 348 of 773 floor votes, or about 45% of all votes, according to the legislature’s records, despite stressing the importance "for leaders to show up" three years later.

Bohannan is running for Congress in Iowa's 1st Congressional District, a race the Cook Political Report ranks as a "toss up" in November as Republicans attempt to preserve their razor-thin majority in the House of Representatives.

Some of the skipped votes involved bills addressing protections for sexual abuse victims, volunteer firefighters and first responders, Iowa’s dairy industry, agricultural programs, emergency 911 services and juvenile justice reform.

IOWA DEM WHO TOUTED 'STRONG WORK ETHIC' MISSES MORE THAN HALF OF HER HOUSE VOTES

"Liberal Christina Bohannan says leaders should ‘show up’ and then is a no-show herself," Emily Tuttle, a spokesperson for the National Republican Congressional Committee, said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Missing half your job while collecting your taxpayer-funded paycheck isn’t leadership worthy of a promotion. It’s the kind of performance that would get you fired anywhere else."

The absences stand in contrast with Bohannan’s past comments. In an Oct. 6, 2025, post on X, she wrote that she had the "honor of speaking" with more than 100 voters at a candidate forum representing five Iowa counties.

"At a time when so much is uncertain, it’s more important than ever for leaders to show up and talk directly with Iowans," she added.

Similarly, in a 2021 interview with Bleeding Heartland, an Iowa politics blog, Bohannan was described as planning to spend "a lot of time on legislative work during the 2022 session" with the rest of her efforts focused on her congressional campaign.

Bohannan served one term in the Iowa House from 2021 to 2023 before launching her first campaign for Congress.

BATTLEGROUND DEM CALLED PATRIOTISM 'SENSITIVE AND CONTROVERSIAL' DURING DEBATE OVER THE PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

She is challenging incumbent Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks, R-Iowa, for a third time in the 1st Congressional District, which includes Davenport and Iowa City, after losing by about seven points in 2022 and roughly 800 votes following a recount in 2024.

But Bohannan remained on the state’s legislative payroll during that period. According to state legislative records, Iowa lawmakers earned a $25,000 annual salary in 2022, plus $175 per day per diem for up to 100 days, or $17,500.

The Democratic lawmaker has also faced mounting criticism for her past comments and middle-class messaging on the campaign trail.

'QUEEN OF DEI' RUNNING FOR CONGRESS RIPPED HER RURAL STATE AS 'BACKWARDS' ON PODCAST

Fox News Digital previously reported that Bohannan warned Iowa could be seen as "backwards" over limits on diversity training at public schools and universities and "look like a backwater" over restrictions on transgender athletes. 

Other reports revealed that Bohannan and her husband owned a waterfront Sarasota, Florida, condo valued between $500,001 and $1 million, in addition to a $1.55 million Iowa City home while campaigning as a hard-working, middle-class advocate who understands what it's like "to still struggle to put food on the table." 

Fox News Digital reached out to Bohannan’s campaign for comment.

item.title: Three-time Olympian Lolo Jones says Team USA 'abandoned' her after harrowing spinal injury
item.description: Lolo Jones says Team USA banned her from the Olympic training center after she demanded medical care for alarming spinal symptoms in Lake Placid.
item.content:encoded:
Lolo Jones is not backing down after a harrowing experience with Team USA.

In February 2025, Jones climbed into a team-issued bobsled at the Olympic training complex in Lake Placid, New York. The U.S. team was testing equipment before the World Championships. The sled accelerated down the ice at speeds approaching 90 mph.

At the bottom of the track, Jones knew something was wrong.

Her lower back burned. She could not bend over. She had lost control of her bladder.

"I’ve never had that happen to me ever in (my) life," Jones said. "I immediately went up to the athletic trainer and told him what was happening."

Jones was no inexperienced athlete struggling to read her body. She competed at the 2008 and 2012 Summer Olympics as a hurdler and the 2014 Winter Olympics as a bobsled brakewoman. She had won world championships in both sports.

She understood pain. This felt different.

SIMONE BILES RETURNS TO HOSPITAL FOR PROCEDURE WEEKS AFTER 'ALMOST DYING' IN 'MEDICAL EMERGENCY'

A trainer arranged a treatment for her, but Jones says the head of sports medicine at the Lake Placid training center canceled it because she had already received treatment that week.

Jones arrived for the appointment without knowing it had been canceled.

She was hurt, frightened and days away from the biggest race of the season. 

TENNESSEE COACH UNLOADS ON NCAA'S 'BULLS–T', AFTER STAR LINEBACKER SUSPENDED FOR OUTDATED RULE

Then Jones received notice that officials had revoked her access to sports medicine, she says, and a broader ban later kept her out of the Olympic training facility, including its rehabilitation areas, weight room, housing and push track.

The notice said her behavior violated the facility’s code of conduct, she says, but Jones claims officials never identified the specific rule she broke or gave her a formal hearing before imposing the punishment.

According to reporting by the Southern California News Group, Jones and other people familiar with the case said USOPC officials later acknowledged that the approved treatment should not have been canceled. Jones apologized during a meeting before the World Championships.

The restrictions remained.

SIMONE BILES FIRES BACK AT INSTAGRAM USERS WHO MOCKED HER NEAR-DEATH EXPERIENCE, REVEALS MEDICAL EMERGENCY

"I voiced my frustration that athletes should have medical access," Jones said. "It just continued to escalate."

The symptoms Jones described demanded more than a routine massage.

Severe back pain combined with bladder dysfunction can signal compression of the nerves at the base of the spinal cord. 

The American Association of Neurological Surgeons lists urinary incontinence, leg weakness and severe lower-back pain among the warning signs of cauda equina syndrome, a medical emergency that can cause permanent paralysis or loss of bladder control.

Jones says no one at the center examined her, ordered imaging or explained the possible severity of her injury.

Without a diagnosis, she made the decision elite athletes often make. She kept going.

Jones obtained pain medication from her doctor in Louisiana and returned to the sled for the World Championships in Lake Placid. She completed four runs with pilot Elana Meyers Taylor. They finished sixth.

"If someone would’ve told me, ‘Your spinal fluid is leaking out of your back. If that pilot hits a wall, you will be paralyzed,’ there is no way I would’ve gotten back in that bobsled," Jones said.

After the championships, Jones paid for her own MRI. She says the imaging revealed a herniated disc, another disc bulge, several lumbar tears and a cerebrospinal-fluid leak. She later underwent spinal surgery.

She also paid for rehabilitation, travel and private medical help while she remained barred from the training center. She estimates the injury and its aftermath cost her about $100,000.

For Jones, the cost exposes a larger imbalance inside Olympic sports.

Many bobsled athletes survive on modest stipends while absorbing significant training and travel expenses. Jones had income from work outside the sport, but she says the bills still devastated her finances.

"I make good money, but I’m not making Michael Phelps money," she said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Jones now argues that Olympic athletes need stronger due-process protections and an affordable way to challenge the institutions that control their medical care, funding and competitive futures. She says the current grievance system costs too much and gives athletes little realistic power against governing bodies.

The experience has also changed how she views the Olympics themselves.

Jones once imagined that a future daughter might follow her into elite sports. She no longer sees that possibility as a dream.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

"I will not let my daughter be an Olympic athlete," she said. "She will not be treated like this."

For more than 20 years, Jones pushed her body for Team USA. She raced through injuries, changed sports and represented the country in both the Summer and Winter Games.

When her body finally forced her to ask for help, she says the system treated her pain as a disciplinary problem.

"I’ve given so much to Team USA and represented this country as best I can," Jones said. "And when I needed Team USA back, they absolutely abandoned me."

item.title: Florida deputy killed ex-girlfriend over a TV, then himself, sheriff says
item.description: Deputy Troy Savetz waited outside his ex-girlfriend's home with a gun, angry over a TV set, before abducting her as her children called 911 from inside.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

A Florida sheriff’s deputy, honored multiple times for his bravery, dedication and compassion, killed a former girlfriend and then himself Monday after an argument over a television.

The victim was identified by friends as Mandy Fackler, who leaves behind two children, 12 and 9, Fox Tampa reported.

Deputy Troy Savetz had been with the Pinellas County Sheriff’s Office for 14 years and was a member of the marine unit.

He and the victim had an "on-again-off-again, tumultuous relationship," Pinellas County Sheriff Bob Gualtieri said in a news conference.

MISSOURI MOM OF 5 FATALLY SHOT WHILE BUYING SLUSHIES WITH CHILDREN; POLICE SEARCH FOR GUNMAN

Savetz, 47, was waiting outside Fackler's home when she and her children returned from a day at the beach at about 5:30 p.m. He brandished a gun and was angry about "wanting his TV set back," Gualtieri said.

When the victim tried to call 911, Savetz took her phone. That’s when she told her two children to go inside.

They did as they were told. And they never saw her again.

The children were "extremely brave," calling 911 and giving dispatchers everything needed to identify the suspect, Pasco County Sheriff Chris Nocco told reporters.

When authorities arrived at the home, they saw the mother’s vehicle with the door wide open, and they found her phone, Nocco said.

"At that point, they realize that she's no longer there" at the residence, he said.

Officers sprang into action using K-9 teams, drones and aviation units, searching for the vehicle Savetz was driving when he carried the victim away, Nocco said.

About 90 minutes after the altercation began, authorities found the vehicle in nearby Spring Hill. Officers approached with a drone and saw two people inside.

When they reached the car on foot, they found Savetz and his victim dead.

"We're not sure when and at what point" he killed her and himself, Nocco said.

The children, now with their biological father, were unharmed in the incident.

DISPATCH AUDIO RELEASED IN MICHIGAN FAMILY MURDER-SUICIDE AS TROUBLED FAMILY'S SECRETS EMERGE

They "should be starting off this week getting ready for school," Nocco said. Instead, they’re "starting off this week getting ready for a sad life without their mother."

He praised the children for their bravery and obedience at such a critical moment.

"I know eventually there's going to be a point in your life where you're going to go back and listen to all the videos and read all the reports," Nocco said.

"So please hear this directly from us: We listened to that 911 tape, and we know that your mother said to go inside to save your lives and to call 911. You did exactly what your mom asked you to do.

"Know this: Your mom is looking down from heaven, and she's so proud of you two … So know that you two did the right thing."

Nocco said officers were "amazed" by the children’s "calmness." The information they provided allowed for the fastest possible response.

"So we're so proud of you, and I know your mom is. But know [that] this entire community is praying for you."

OFF-DUTY TROOPER AND ARMED CITIZEN HAILED AS HEROES AFTER RETURNING FIRE ON IN-N-OUT GUNMAN

Before this, Savetz had earned accolades for his behavior while wearing the badge. In 2014, he was honored by the sheriff’s office for his "heroic action" in saving the life of a 24-year-old man, stopping him from jumping off a bridge in Pinellas County.

That earned him attention from the Tampa Bay Rays baseball team, who called him "Our Everyday MVP" in a June 2015 social media post. Wearing his green uniform, Savetz was honored by receiving the opportunity to throw out a ceremonial first pitch.

He was hailed a "hero" at local fundraisers and by radio stations.

In 2018, the sheriff’s office shared a social media post about how Savetz had adopted a pot-bellied pig he found while on duty. That year, he and Maple, as she became known, went on to be named ambassadors for the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals in Tampa Bay.

But the "inexcusable" behavior of Savetz immediately ended his identity as a law enforcement officer, Gualtieri said.

"The moment this individual committed a crime, he was no longer a law enforcement officer. He was a criminal."

item.title: Pittsburgh Pirates vs. Miami Marlins betting preview: why the over 8 is the play tonight
item.description: Carmen Mlodzinski and Janson Junk take the mound as the Pittsburgh Pirates and Miami Marlins battle for NL Wild Card positioning in mid-August.
item.content:encoded:
We are about halfway through August, and there are some teams that really need to make a push if they plan to have a true run at a postseason spot. We've seen some very hot and very cold stretches from a variety of teams this season, so who will be next? The National League has its divisions essentially set with the Dodgers, Braves, and Brewers looking like they will coast to the finish line. Both the Pirates and the Marlins are hoping to steal one of those remaining Wild Card spots.

The Pittsburgh Pirates seem to have ebbed and flowed all season. There were stretches where they looked like one of the better teams in the league. Their hitting issues that were addressed in the offseason have been significantly better this year. However, their pitching has struggled. Even their superstar, Paul Skenes, has had a bit of a down year. His numbers are still strong, but they are the worst of his young career. If the Pirates can get some performances out of their other starters, they might have a hot streak left in them.

One guy that they need to step up is today's hurler, Carmen Mlodzinski. For the year, Mlodzinski is 6-4 for the year with a 3.51 ERA and a 1.36 WHIP. He has been better on the road with a 3.10 ERA, and he has started two more games on the road. However, he has just 1.1 more innings on the road than at home this year. Mlodzinski is essentially an opener for the Pirates. He hasn't thrown more than three innings in any of his past 12 outings (varying between starts and relief appearances). Marlins hitters have only gotten four at-bats against him, but all four hitters went 0-for-1.

The Miami Marlins have quietly put together a good campaign. You wouldn't really know it because in this division almost everyone will get more attention than them. It doesn't help that the franchise seems to always trade away any good player and doesn't invest in their team. Maybe that's more of a personal thought or frustration. In any case, the Marlins are 61-59 for the season and have been great at home. With the Braves and Phillies ahead of them, and the Mets being major markets, it is possible to lose sight of the Marlins.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Today they send out some Junk to the mound. Bad jokes aside, Janson Junk takes the hill for Miami today. For the season, Junk is sitting with a 5-7 record and a 4.63 ERA. He has just 62 strikeouts and a 1.36 WHIP over 81.2 innings. Most of the damage has been done by hits instead of walks, so there isn't much of a control issue. He doesn't pitch much more than five innings, typically. He hasn't thrown more than five innings in any of his last eight outings. Aside from a six-run outing in July, he also hasn't allowed more than two earned runs in a start since May 25th (he missed all of June). Pirates hitters are 3-for-8 against Junk.

This should be a game where we get some offense and some action. Neither pitcher is in a category where I would call them un-hittable. Neither team is likely to have their starter/opener go too deep into the game, either. Miami does have a better bullpen than Pittsburgh, so that might be a reason to bet on them to win, but I think we see more than eight runs scored in this game. Give me the Marlins and Pirates over 8 tonight.

item.title: Tafoya makes 'common sense' pitch to disaffected Democrats as she vows to fight Minnesota’s ‘socialist lurch’
item.description: Michele Tafoya won the Minnesota GOP Senate primary and now faces Peggy Flanagan, pitching common sense to voters across the political spectrum.
item.content:encoded:
EDINA, MN - As socialist candidates continue to score victories across the country and take more control of the Democratic Party, Minnesota GOP Senate nominee Michele Tafoya is making her pitch to voters from all parties who still believe in "common sense."

"We do not want to see a socialist lurch anywhere in this country, and in particular in Minnesota, so I will do whatever I can to stand up against this movement toward Democrat socialism," Tafoya told Fox News Digital on Tuesday shortly after voting in a suburb outside Minneapolis. "Socialism does not work."

"So I actually moved to rural Washington because I could buy this pretty house, and it wasn't very expensive in comparison to living in LA for all those years," she said. "The permission came from my children being old enough that they live somewhere else. You know, they go to college, they live in other states, and I know women always talk about empty nest syndrome, and mine was unique," Farr began. "I didn't leave LA for 15 years when I had babies. I was afraid of working out of town. I was afraid of missing everything. I was afraid to do a one-hour drama."

item.title: Grocery boss warns Mamdani's city-run stores pit government against 'its own citizens'
item.description: Gristedes CEO warns New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's $70 million city-run grocery stores will devastate bodegas and supermarkets nearby.
item.content:encoded:
As New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani moves ahead with a plan to open five city-run grocery stores, one of the Big Apple’s biggest supermarket owners has a blunt warning: the stores won't feed the hungry, but they will shelve the bodegas next door.

"The fact is the people [Mamdani] is going to hurt are the current bodegas or the current supermarkets in those neighborhoods," John Catsimatidis, CEO of the New York City grocery chain Gristedes, told Fox News Digital. "So it becomes a problem of ‘for whom do the bells toll?’"

In July, Mamdani announced the stores would be located in each of the city’s five boroughs, with the first location set to open in Hunts Point in the Bronx in late 2027. The mayor added he hopes to have all five stores operational before his term ends in 2030, and has set the project’s capital budget at an eye-watering $70 million.

MAMDANI’S CITY GROCERY PLAN COULD LEAVE TAXPAYERS PAYING FOR EVERY BANANA

The government-run shops will offer a 30% discount on a "core basket of everyday groceries," including meat, seafood and fresh produce, in an attempt to combat the affordability crisis plaguing the city, according to Mamdani’s administration.

"Every week, New Yorkers walk into a grocery store hoping the prices haven’t gone up again. A trip to the grocery store shouldn’t spell dread for New Yorkers," Mamdani said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani’s administration for comment.

The city is currently accepting applications from private operators interested in managing the logistical challenges of running the stores. Mamdani’s administration has also vowed to cover the property taxes and rental costs for each location — a decision that Catsimatidis feels puts local business owners at a disadvantage.

NY GOVERNOR HOPEFUL VOWS SHOWDOWN WITH MAMDANI OVER SOCIALIST AGENDA: ‘I WILL STOP HIM’

"The people that are going to run those five stores are not going to pay any real estate taxes. Not going to pay any rent," Catsimatidis said. "If I don’t pay any rent or real estate taxes, I can bring down the cost of a product 20% across the board."

In recent years, business owners throughout the five boroughs have been faced with expanding hurdles taking aim at their bottom line.

Catsimatidis added that local owners are already dealing with increased competition from outside vendors who rely on online commerce to reach consumers in the Big Apple, with the average grocery store operating at just a 1% to 3% profit margin.

GROCER-TURNED-LAWMAKER SAYS MAMDANI’S GOVERNMENT-RUN STORES 'MIGHT NOT EVEN LAST A YEAR'

"The businesses that are doing business outside New York City are just shipping [products] in by mail, they can afford to be cheaper," Catsimatidis said. "And you know what happens? They put the stores and the businesses inside New York City out of business."

According to the grocery tycoon, new and increasing costs — including congestion pricing and the rising cost of electricity — are also cutting business owners in New York City off at the knees.

"The big picture is that five stores in five boroughs is only good for public relations, and it's not really going to help the hungry," Catsimatidis told Fox News Digital. "Congestion pricing is hurting the stores in Manhattan a great deal. If you go up and down the streets in New York City, half the stores are empty — which is horrible."

Catsimatidis pointed out that Manhattan’s congestion pricing — which was enacted in January 2025 — puts a premium on deliveries traveling south of 61st Street.

"If I want stuff delivered to us from vendors in New Jersey — and all these companies are in New Jersey, Nassau, Suffolk County, Brooklyn, Queens or the Bronx — and I say to them, ‘I want you to deliver to New York City,' they're going to charge me 10% more, or 15% more," Catsimatidis said.

I WATCHED CHICAGO PROMISE FOOD EQUITY. NOW MY NEIGHBORHOOD HAS EMPTY SHELVES

While the solution to rolling out affordable grocery options without infringing on businesses within the area isn’t necessarily black and white, Catsimatidis is offering his own suggestion on how Mamdani’s administration can walk the line.

"If they’re not given credits to reduce their prices, then they’re going to be hurting," Catsimatidis said. "If you want me to lower the price of eggs, well maybe I’ll lower the price of the eggs by a dollar a dozen. But maybe [the city] will give me a dollar a dozen credit toward my real estate taxes."

"If you want to lower the prices for all Americans, all New Yorkers, well let’s do it right and lower it in all five boroughs," he added.

While Mamdani’s rollout of the city-run grocery stores has not come without critics, director of the CUNY Urban Food Policy Institute Nevin Cohen emphasized New York City’s dire need for officials to combat food insecurity among its residents.

THE OVERLOOKED WAY THE IRAN WAR IS MAKING GROCERIES, AMAZON PACKAGES AND NEW HOMES MORE EXPENSIVE

"The problem is that many people can’t afford food for their families," Cohen told Fox News Digital. "1.4 million New Yorkers are food insecure, which means that they’re unsure whether they have enough money to put food on the table. Twenty percent of New Yorkers depend on SNAP benefits or federal food subsidies to put food on the table for the family."

Cohen also pointed to an existing program titled "FRESH," which aims to identify food deserts within New York City.

"It provides tax incentives and zoning incentives to encourage new supermarkets or the expansion of existing supermarkets in neighborhoods deemed to be underserved by food retail," Cohen said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

While Catsimatidis agrees the city-run grocery stores are being placed in neighborhoods throughout the city that would serve lower-income residents, he remains worried about the impact the shops will have on businesses in the immediate area, while pointing to Mamdani’s democratic socialist platform.

"You're competing against your own citizens, and that's only done in socialist countries," Catsimatidis told Fox News Digital. "Look at socialist countries — nobody's breaking down the walls to get in, but they're all breaking down the walls to get into the United States of America."

item.title: New power axis in the making? Three military heavyweights lock arms, complicating Abraham Accords strategy
item.description: The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan raises questions about whether it signals a Middle East shift from the U.S.
item.content:encoded:
A new defense pact linking Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan is fueling debate over whether the three countries are laying the groundwork for a competing regional bloc — potentially challenging the U.S.-backed architecture built around Israel and the Abraham Accords — or simply creating a new model of burden-sharing among American partners.

The three countries, all with longstanding security ties to the United States, enter the pact with different interests — but together they could begin shifting the region’s balance of power.

Saudi Arabia signed a Strategic Defense Agreement with the United States in November 2025 and was designated a major non-NATO ally, but Riyadh did not secure the treaty-level, Article 5-style U.S. defense guarantee it had long sought, making the new pact a potential hedge against uncertainty over Washington’s future security commitments.

Pakistan, a nuclear-armed state, gains greater energy security, Saudi investment and regional influence, while offering significant military capabilities — although whether its nuclear deterrent extends to its partners remains unconfirmed. Turkey, already a NATO member, gains a larger market for its growing defense industry and additional strategic weight as tensions with Israel rise.

WHO IS TURKEY'S RECEP TAYYIP ERDOĞAN? HOW NATO'S MOST UNPREDICTABLE LEADER KEEPS REINVENTING HIMSELF

Taken together, the arrangement gives three U.S. partners greater ability to build deterrence on their own — potentially easing Washington’s security burden while also giving them more independence from it.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on Aug. 7. A joint statement said the pact was intended to "strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression" and stipulated that an armed attack against one country would be regarded as an attack against all three.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan went further the following day, telling Turkey’s state-run Anadolu news agency that the agreement was "technically the same" as NATO’s Article 5 mutual-defense provision, which treats an attack on one member as an attack on all. Fidan said, however, that the countries would consult on the degree and form of assistance provided following an attack, with operational details still to be determined by a new ministerial committee. The alliance will also establish a general secretariat based in Saudi Arabia, Reuters reported Aug. 8.

Fidan said President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan wants the alliance to eventually expand beyond its three founding members and identified Egypt as a potential participant. He said negotiations over the pact had been underway for two years and eight months.

Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly has pushed back on suggestions that the agreement represents the creation of a new sectarian or military bloc, saying it is not connected to nuclear ambitions or an arms race. Turkish officials have similarly said the pact is defensive and not directed against Iran or any other country.

Iran, meanwhile, played down the pact as a threat to Tehran. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Aug. 10 that Iran saw no reason to be concerned that the agreement was directed against it, telling Reuters that the pact reflected a regional shift toward countries relying more heavily on their own security capabilities rather than outside powers.

"Any plan that is based on the geopolitical and historical realities of the region, is comprehensive and inclusive, and correctly identifies the enemy and the threat, has a chance of helping to strengthen security and prevent instability and abuses by the Zionist enemy and its allies," Baghaei said, referring to Israel.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Turkish Embassy in Washington, D.C., and the Pakistani government for comment but did not receive responses in time for publication.

Sinan Ciddi, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies and director of its Turkey program, told Fox News Digital that he remains skeptical that the pact currently amounts to a NATO-style alliance.

AMERICANS ARE NOT GIVING UP ON NATO, BUT THEY EXPECT EUROPE TO DO ITS SHARE

"Does it have teeth? Is it a serious deterrent? Is that a serious collective defense pact? Is it a Muslim NATO? We're not actually sure yet," Ciddi said.

Ciddi said each of the three countries enters the pact with different incentives. For Saudi Arabia, he sees it as a hedge against doubts over the reliability of U.S. security guarantees; for Pakistan, it offers greater energy security, Saudi investment and added regional prestige; and for Turkey, it creates new opportunities for defense cooperation and a larger market for its arms industry. Ankara also gains additional deterrent weight as its tensions with Israel grow, he argued.

"I would say that this pact is much more targeted towards closer economic and commercial ties rather than substantive NATO-like security ties," Ciddi added.

Saudi Arabia rejects the suggestion that the agreement represents a turn away from Washington.

WATCH: DEMOCRATS BLAST TRUMP SAUDI NUCLEAR DEAL AS GOP TOUTS REGIONAL ALLIANCE

"The United States remains to be our primary strategic partner," a Saudi source told Fox News Digital on background, saying the kingdom’s expanding ties with Pakistan and Turkey should not be viewed as coming at the expense of its relationship with Washington.

The Saudi source also rejected descriptions of the agreement as a "Muslim NATO" or Sunni alliance and said it was not directed against Israel, Iran or any other particular country. Asked whether the pact represented a Saudi move away from normalization with Israel, the source said, "It's not related in any way."

Aziz Alghashian, a senior non-resident fellow at the Gulf International Forum, offered a similar interpretation.

"I don't think it's a counterweight to the Abraham Accords," Alghashian told Fox News Digital.

WHY NATO’S DEFENSE SPENDING IMBALANCE LASTED FOR DECADES

Instead, Alghashian described the agreement as part of Saudi Arabia’s longer-term diversification of strategic relationships.

"I think it's actually a supplementation. It's complementary to the United States," he said, arguing that greater cooperation among regional partners could provide increased burden-sharing for Washington.

From Pakistan’s perspective, the agreement offers both military and political advantages, Raza Rumi, distinguished lecturer at the Roosevelt House Public Policy Institute at CUNY, told Fox News Digital.

"Pakistan gains strategic depth, greater leverage in the Gulf and a more formal place in an emerging regional security architecture," Rumi said, pointing to potential cooperation on defense production, technology transfers, intelligence, training and air and missile defense.

But he cautioned against interpreting the pact’s mutual-defense language too literally.

"Seriously, but not literally as an Article 5-style guarantee, at least not yet," Rumi said. Its credibility, he added, will depend on whether the countries develop joint planning, command structures and procedures for responding to crises.

Rumi also warned against assuming the Middle East is already dividing into two fixed camps. India, however, is watching the new alignment closely. India’s Ministry of External Affairs said Aug. 11 that it was examining the pact’s implications for national security and regional peace and stability, adding that New Delhi would take "whatever necessary steps are required" to safeguard its interests.

"These states are hedging, not choosing permanent blocs," he said.

TRUMP SQUEEZED BETWEEN ISRAEL AND TURKEY AS NETANYAHU, ERDOGAN ESCALATE FEUD

Ciddi, on the other hand, argued that the agreement reflects "serious reservations" among regional countries about U.S. security guarantees. His greater concern is that even a militarily weak pact could encourage opposing alignments to harden.

"Security pacts beget more security pacts," Ciddi said, arguing that Israel, Greece, Cyprus and potentially India could deepen their own cooperation in response.

"You're buying security, but you're also creating tension," he said. "That's where I think the harm comes in."

Calling the pact a direct counterweight to the Abraham Accords or the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor would therefore be "premature," Rumi argued. But he said a broader competition is emerging over the region’s future — between U.S.-backed economic integration involving India, Israel and the Gulf and efforts by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan to develop greater strategic autonomy.

item.content:encoded:
Golf: the only sport in which the fans care more about the regular season than the playoffs. In fact, most of you thought the PGA TOUR 2026 season ended after the final major, the British Open. But, nope. The FedExCup Playoffs start this week with the FedEx St. Jude Championship at TPC Southwind in Memphis, Tennessee.

Only the top 69 golfers in the FedExCup standings head to Memphis for the first round of the playoffs because Daniel Berger withdrew. With no cut and massive playoff points at stake, only the top 50 in the standings advance to next week's BMW Championship.

PAR TALK: INCREDIBLE MICHAEL BLOCK DRAMA, YOUNG AMERICAN STREAK CONTINUES ON PGA TOUR AND JOAQUIN NIEMANN DOES IT AGAIN

TPC Southwind is a 7,288-yard, par-70 that rewards precise iron play more than mindless bombing. Water is in play throughout; the Bermuda greens can get tricky, and missed approaches bring bogey into the equation quickly. Hence, I'm upweighting ball-striking and course management in my handicap.

My betting strategy for the St. Jude Championship is to wager enough on a golfer's outright to profit 20 units (u), while backing them up with top-10 and 20 bets. That said, let's talk about the guys I'm backing in the first round of the FedExCup Playoffs.

2026 FedEx St. Jude Championship Best Bets

The following odds are from when I bet on the golfers listed below. Subject to change.

🇯🇵 Hideki Matsuyama +3300 (0.61u) at DraftKings and Top-10 with ties +240 (0.5u) at Kalshi

🇳🇴 Viktor Hovland +4356 (0.46u) at Kalshi and Top-10 with ties +275 (0.5u) at BetMGM

🇺🇸 Justin Thomas +5146 (0.39u) at Polymarket and Top-10 with ties +275 (0.5u) at BetMGM

🇰🇷 Tom Kim +5500 (0.36u) at DraftKings and Top-20 with ties +146 (0.75u) at Kalshi

🇺🇸 Rickie Fowler +8481 (0.24u) at Polymarket and Top-20 with ties +189 (0.75u) at Kalshi

‘Deki has five straight T20-or-better finishes at TPC Southwind, and I cashed on him when he won the 2024 St. Jude Championship at +3000. Furthermore, he has the best course history in this field, according to Betsperts Golf’s Ron Klos.

Matsuyama has five consecutive T14-or-better finishes entering the 2026 St. Jude, with a T3 (3M Open), T5 (Rocket Classic) and T7 (Wyndham Championship) in his last three tournaments.

Hideki has gained strokes on the field in driving accuracy in six consecutive starts, has picked up strokes putting in four of his last five outings, has a world-class short-game and is dialed in with his irons.

Between his skill set and the course history/fit, Matsuyama should have a shorter price than many names ahead of him on the betting board, so I’m taking the value.

I’m probably missing something, but Hovland shouldn’t have worse odds here than Patrick Cantlay and Si Woo Kim, who haven’t won this season, or in the last couple of seasons for that matter.

Hovland won the 2026 Travelers Championship at another TPC course (River Highlands) three starts back and nearly won the 2024 St. Jude by finishing T2.

Iron play is a separator at TPC Southwind, and Hovland has gained strokes on approach in all four majors this year and eight straight starts. Viktor is a notoriously crappy chipper, but around-the-green is deemphasized at TPC Southwind.

Regardless, as long as he plays his game this weekend — dialed in with his irons and accurate off-the-tee — Hovland will be in the mix on Sunday.

Okay, so JT is down to +3605 at Polymarket now, and I'm sorry. But I gave out my full betting card for the St. Jude via X/Twitter Monday, and I've only hit one outright this season. Meaning, if you don't want to bet Thomas at the current odds, it's a good thing you didn't see it on X.

Also, I'm not even sure why JT's number has come down so far. I know why I bet him, and I'll get into that in a second. However, DataGolf.com, which is like scripture in the golf betting community, makes his true odds +2975. Bookmaker, the sharpest sportsbook for golf, has Thomas at +3002 as of Wednesday at midnight.

Back to why I bet JT. He's won the 2020 St. Jude Invitational, and a couple of his 14 other PGA TOUR wins have come at similar courses with a ton of water hazards, such as TPC Sawgrass (THE 2021 PLAYERS Championship) and PGA National (The 2018 Honda Classic).

Thomas gained strokes on approach in his six visits to TPC Southwind. His biggest weakness is driving accuracy, and he hit a higher rate of fairways than the field in nine of his last 10 starts, including four straight, per DataGolf.com.

JT has played well this season — eight top-20 finishes, highlighted by a T4 at the 2026 PGA Championship — and if he can stay out of the water, he should play much better this week than his odds indicate.

The South Korean cashed a big top-20 bet for me last week by tying for fifth at the Wyndham Championship, so I'm happy to reinvest that money back into him this week. Kim won the 2026 Genesis Scottish Open four starts back, two weeks after nearly winning the U.S. Open, where he finished third.

More importantly, his game is a perfect fit for this course. Because of all the water, accuracy off-the-tee and with your irons is important at TPC Southwind, and Kim is one of the most precise ball-strikers in the world. He ranks second in this field for Strokes Gained (SG): Approach over the last 40 rounds, per Bet The Number.

Kim has gained strokes with his irons and in driving accuracy in all three St. Judes from 2022-24. He's picked up strokes on approach in 15 of his last 16 starts, including 11 straight, according to DataGolf.com. Fowler has had a roller coaster season, but he comes into the St. Jude with strong lead-in form. He has 10 top-20 finishes in 19 events this season, including three straight: T15 at the John Deere Classic, T18 at the British Open and T8 at the Rocket Classic.
